verdict.rationale: USCIS documents a self-service online account that can be created and accessed remotely from a computer, phone, or tablet. Representatives also use their own online accounts to file on behalf of clients, which suggests a remote credential-based sign-in an authorized human can complete. The evidence never describes the authentication mechanism itself, so the MFA element is not established, and nothing explicitly rules out biometric, in-person, or mailed-PIN identity steps. missing for 10: documentation that sign-in uses credential MFA (e.g., authenticator app/SMS/email codes), explicit confirmation that no biometric liveness, in-person visit, or mailed PIN is required for account setup or sign-in, independent or hands-on corroboration of the sign-in flow
